EXPECTED_SIGN: positive

NAME: Knowledge Operating Leverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(MUL(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ebitda, sale), 1), 1))))

EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Margin expansion following prior knowledge accumulation captures intangible scalability: additional commercialization produces operating income without proportionate tangible input. Requiring a high cash-flow yield distinguishes underpriced operating leverage from expensive innovation firms already valued for that payoff.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Booked Intangible Efficiency Recovery
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), IND_RANK(MUL(LAG(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(revt, at), 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are cheap on enterprise EBITDA yield outperform when a meaningful recognized-intangible base is accompanied by improving revenue productivity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Weighting the change in revenue-to-assets by prior intangible intensity measures productivity improvement without dividing by a potentially tiny intangible balance. Treating the absence of a reported recognized-intangible balance as zero preserves coverage while preventing non-intangible firms from dominating the productivity channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Unstable Research Margin Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho)))), MUL(IND_RANK(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Expensive firms with unstable R&D policies and deteriorating gross margins earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: R&D instability alone produced an expected-sign Fama-MacBeth slope but a wrong-sign portfolio alpha, plausibly because volatile successful innovators entered the extreme portfolio. Gross-margin deterioration adds evidence that the instability reflects failed commercialization rather than productive experimentation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Balance-Sheet-Backed Knowledge Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sales-cheap, R&D-intensive firms outperform when low net leverage gives them the capacity to sustain intangible investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Intangible assets provide weak collateral, so leverage can turn apparent cheapness into financing distress and destabilize the long portfolio. The net-leverage condition retains persistent innovators whose valuation discount is less likely to reflect an inability to fund future research.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Post-Research Harvest State
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MUL(IND_RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: EBITDA-cheap firms outperform when R&D intensity has receded from its historical peak while sales productivity is near the top of its own history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Distance from peak R&D identifies firms moving beyond the investment phase, while a high historical position in sales-to-assets confirms that the decline is harvesting rather than research abandonment. This state-based construction may form more stable portfolios than relying on one-period changes in R&D and sales.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
